what_it_does: Graph partitioning—dividing a circuit graph into balanced regions—is a core step in chip design and optimization. As engineers iteratively improve a circuit, the graph changes slightly with each edit, but existing GPU accelerators re-partition the entire graph from scratch each time, wasting computation. iG-kway is the first GPU-accelerated graph partitioner that tracks which parts of the graph changed and only re-partitions the affected regions, similar to how incremental compilation in software development avoids recompiling unchanged code. This dramatically speeds up the CAD (computer-aided design) optimization loop.
